cautions: FRAMEWORK FIDELITY: the four management functions (plan-organize-lead-control), the classic leadership-style taxonomies (autocratic/democratic/laissez-faire), Maslow/Hertzberg/McClelland motivation theories, Tuckman's team stages, the Thomas-Kilmann conflict modes, SMART goals — all standard textbook material; attribute to canonical sources (OpenStax, original theorists via reliable secondary). Never present a framework as invented.
THEORY NOT OPINION: motivation/leadership theories taught factually ('Maslow's hierarchy proposes...') — no pop-psychology, no '5 secrets of great leaders' content.
NO ADVICE: performance-management teaches the process; employee-engagement teaches what it is and what drives it; nothing prescriptive for the reader's own job.
DIVERSITY & INCLUSION: factual (what D&I is, why organizations pursue it, the business/legal case named generally); EEOC facts U.S.-labeled; no policy positions.
ETHICS: management ethics (ethics vs compliance, ethical dilemmas) — the philosophy subject owns ethical theory depth (reference only).
Psychology overlaps (motivation, organizational-behavior) — the psychology subject owns psychological depth (reference only).
